details: Read shared context (tilize focus shape [1,1,32,16384], reader stage 33% of op, 4678ns), tilize_reader.cpp reader_read_block branch, read_sticks_for_tilize helper, TensorAccessor interleaved addressing (dataflow_api_addrgen.h: 12 non-pow2 DRAM banks -> udivsi3_const_divisor per stick), noc_async_read_one_packet_set_state/with_state semantics (set_state writes COORD+LEN, with_state writes LO+LO+CTRL -- naive per-stick state reuse saves nothing since bank changes every stick; grouping by bank is required for real savings). Used tt-probe to get exact derive_plan block params for 5 domain shapes via pd.derive_plan. Scaffolding bench off ttnn/ttnn/operations/examples/noc_placement (CBDescriptor/KernelDescriptor/generic_op pattern).

Noticed sibling perf_experiments dirs already present (reader_bank_rotate, writer_bank_rotate, writer_dual_risc, writer_state_reuse, short_wide_block_width) -- other part-optimizers in this tournament round. Left them untouched. Built bench.py (host ProgramDescriptor, scaffolded off examples/noc_placement) + 5 reader kernel variants (helper/raw/recurrence/state_naive/state_grouped) + shared writer_block.cpp + test_bench.py. Domain shapes block params probed exactly via pd.derive_plan on device: focus(32,512,1x64) wide_short(32,512,1x64 truncated from 128) square(64,512,16x4) tall_narrow(256,64,64x1) small(32,64,1x64). About to run correctness smoke test on helper/focus.

Hit a CB reserve_back deadlock on rows_per_block>32 shapes (square rows=64, tall_narrow rows=256): read_sticks_for_tilize internally chunks into 32-stick reserve/read/barrier/push cycles when total_num_rows>tile_h, but my raw/recurrence/state_naive/state_grouped kernels + writer originally did ONE reserve/push for the whole block, sized for only bw pages -> CB too small, second internal chunk blocked forever. Fixed by restructuring all 4 non-helper reader kernels + writer_block.cpp to loop over num_chunks=rows/32 tile-row chunks, matching the helper baseline granularity exactly (fair apples-to-apples comparison), with the recurrence/grouped-state logic re-derived fresh per chunk (one division per 32-stick chunk instead of per whole block -- still the same idea, just correctly scoped). All 25 correctness cases (5 variants x 5 shapes) now PASS bit-identity.

3 independent --profile runs (25 cases x 3) + zone_report.py breakdowns. Zone-level diagnosis: reader stage is barrier-dominant on 32-row blocks (issue ~28-30%, barrier ~67-68%) but issue-dominant on tiny-transfer blocks (small shape: issue 60-71%, barrier 20-28%) and reserve-dominant-via-CB-wait on many-chunk blocks (tall_narrow: single-buffered CB makes reserve a wait-for-writer artifact, not real cost -- flagged as a bench limitation). recurrence: real, repeatable issue-cost reduction every shape (issue zone -2.5% to -23% vs raw) but only clears the whole-op noise band on tall_narrow (many small reads): median -5.8% vs raw, -4.6% vs helper, repeatable across 3 runs. Flat-to-noise (+-4%) elsewhere. state_naive: flat-to-worse everywhere (+1.7% to +10.8% vs raw), confirms naive per-stick set_state/with_state saves nothing when bank changes almost every call (12 banks). state_grouped (the real idea 3+4 candidate): clean, repeatable REGRESSION on every shape (+4.4% to +23.4% vs raw, +5.8% to +24.6% vs helper) -- the 12-way bank-group bookkeeping (branches, per-bank first-row compare) costs more than the register-write savings it was meant to buy, even on tall_narrow (256 reads/12banks, the most favorable case for grouping). All 25 correctness cases still pass bit-identity after these measurements (unchanged from correctness pass). Verdict: REGRESSION for the main idea (state reuse, naive or grouped); recurrence alone is a narrow, real WIN confined to high-stick-count blocks. Writing up final report now.
